O infinitivo com zu, passo a passo: The infinitive with zu, step by step
PASSO 1: depois de MUITOS verbos, adjeti: STEP 1: after MANY verbs, adjectives and expressions, the second verb goes in the INFINITIVE with «ZU» before it — just like English "to": «Ich versuche, Deutsch zu lernen» (I'm trying to learn German). STEP 2: «zu» comes RIGHT BEFORE the infinitive, at the end of the sentence; add a comma when the infinitive has other words with it: «Ich habe vergessen, dich anzurufen» (I forgot to call you). STEP 3: with SEPARABLE verbs, «zu» goes BETWEEN the prefix and the verb, all one word: anrufen → «anzurufen», mitbringen → «mitzubringen», aufstehen → «aufzustehen». STEP 4: verbs that take «zu»: anfangen, aufhören, beginnen, versuchen, vergessen, vorhaben, hoffen, planen, vorschlagen, empfehlen. Many match English "to"-verbs: try to, forget to, hope to, plan to. STEP 5: expressions with «zu»: «Ich habe Lust / Zeit / keine Lust, … zu …» (I feel like / have time / don't feel like…), «Es ist wichtig / schön / schwer, … zu …» (it's important / nice / hard to…). STEP 6: compare with the modals — the same as English "can" without "to": «Ich kann schwimmen» (no zu) × «Ich versuche zu schwimmen» (with zu).
o português usa «a/de/para» + infinitivo: English puts "to" before the infinitive ("I forgot to call"). German does the same with «zu», but at the END of the sentence: «Ich habe vergessen, dich anzurufen». And where English modals take no "to" (can, must, will), German modals take no «zu» either.
Ich habe vergessen, dich zu anrufen.

Infinitivo sem zu, passo a passo: The infinitive without zu, step by step
PASSO 1: os MODAIS não levam «zu»: «Ich: STEP 1: the MODALS don't take «zu»: «Ich kann schwimmen», «Ich muss arbeiten». STEP 2: neither does «werden» (Futur I): «Ich werde kommen.» STEP 3: verbs of going and staying, without «zu» — English uses "-ing" here: «Ich gehe schwimmen» (I'm going swimming), «Ich bleibe sitzen» (I stay seated), «Wir fahren einkaufen» (we're going shopping). STEP 4: «lassen» (to have something done, to let), «sehen» and «hören» (to see/hear an action): «Ich lasse das Auto reparieren» (I'm having the car repaired), «Ich sehe ihn kommen» (I see him coming), «Ich höre sie singen» (I hear her singing). STEP 5: «helfen» and «lernen» usually go without «zu» with a short infinitive: «Ich helfe dir kochen», «Ich lerne schwimmen». STEP 6: if in DOUBT, check the list: modal, werden, lassen, gehen, bleiben, sehen, hören → no «zu»; anfangen, versuchen, vergessen, hoffen → «zu».

Infinitivo com zu em conversas de planos: The infinitive with zu when talking about plans and habits
PASSO 1: para planos: «Ich habe vor, im: STEP 1: for plans: «Ich habe vor, im Sommer nach Berlin zu fahren» (I'm planning to go to Berlin this summer). STEP 2: to suggest: «Hast du Lust, am Wochenende wandern zu gehen?» (Do you feel like going hiking this weekend?) STEP 3: for new habits: «Ich habe begonnen, jeden Morgen zu joggen» (I've started jogging every morning). STEP 4: to remind and to forget: «Vergiss nicht, deine Schuhe mitzubringen!» (Don't forget to bring your shoes!) STEP 5: to be clear and concise: use «zu + infinitive» instead of «dass» when the subject is the same: «Ich hoffe, dich bald zu sehen» (I hope to see you soon) instead of «Ich hoffe, dass ich dich bald sehe».
